answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond and files one key-hashed pigment assay in a public lantern registry, which refuses any assay hash already filed. Auditors replay the registry each epoch, and a sable seal binds each filing to its key, so a copied or rented assay burns the bond. One thousand fakes pay 1,000 x 115 = 115,000 credits against a 40,000 pool. An honest agent pays 45 once and keeps its full share.
